body: A hype post asserting a cartoon AI ad ran 66 days and converts even though viewers know it's AI; links a 278-ad board of AI animations as the proof set.

idea: You don't have to hide that an ad is AI — acknowledged fakeness still converts, so the animation format is a marketer's paradise.
sequencing: Longevity proof: 66 days active on one cartoon AI ad.
Thesis: people know it's not real and STILL BUY.
Mechanism: acknowledged fakeness removes the realism burden, freeing pure novelty.

formatting: Short punchy text post; no media pulled. Authority-curator voice.
why_it_works: Collapses the main objection to AI creative ("it looks fake") into the selling point: the 66-day run is the receipt.
what_to_steal: The permission slip: LC can run openly-AI animation without chasing photorealism — the format's permission to be fake is the creative advantage, especially for mechanism/x-ray storytelling where realism isn't the point.

product: Frequency-healing device (brand not named in file)
hook: "What if I told you there's a frequency that breaks apart blood clots in seconds?"
body: A teardown of a frequency-healing device's ad that ran unchanged for 198 days: 3 minutes 40 seconds of sales-letter text scrolling over ONE looping CGI shot inside a blood vessel. Opens on "What if I told you there's a frequency that breaks apart blood clots in seconds?" and closes on stock scarcity: "if you see a button below, that means it's in stock right now." Works with sound off; cost one CGI clip.
cta: "If you see a button below, that means it's in stock right now" — scarcity-as-inventory CTA, plus a swipe-file link in the curator's post.
idea: One looping hyperreal CGI shot + scrolling sales-letter text = a 198-day winner that costs almost nothing to produce.
sequencing: Hook: the frequency/blood-clot question over a blood-vessel CGI loop.
Mechanism: sales-letter text explains how the frequency works (scrolling, sound-off).
Proof/visual: the same hypnotic interior-body shot loops for 3:40.
Urgency: stock scarcity tied to the button's visibility.
CTA: buy while the button is there.
formatting: 3:41 long-form video: static looping CGI blood-vessel shot + scrolling sales-letter text overlay. No speaker, sound-off friendly.
why_it_works: Radical production simplicity + hypnotic loop: the brain stays for the motion, the text does the selling, and sound-off compatibility captures the silent majority of feed viewers.
what_to_steal: The cheapest possible LC version: one looping macro CGI shot (water beading on PVD coating, x-ray of clasp mechanism) + scrolling benefit text, sound-off, run for months — a near-zero-cost evergreen creative for retargeting.
